claim: The global health burden due to sepsis and the associated cytokine storm is substantial.
source: The global health burden due to sepsis and the associated cytokine storm is substantial.
evidence: This is a general statement supported by citations in the introduction section referencing CDC and Singer et al., 2016.

claim: Early intervention has improved survival during the cytokine storm.
source: While early intervention has improved survival during the cytokine storm, those that survive can enter a state of chronic immunoparalysis defined by transient lymphopenia and functional deficits of surviving cells.
evidence: Supported by citations in the introduction discussing mortality rate reductions.

claim: Sepsis survivors can enter a state of chronic immunoparalysis defined by transient lymphopenia and functional deficits of surviving cells.
source: While early intervention has improved survival during the cytokine storm, those that survive can enter a state of chronic immunoparalysis defined by transient lymphopenia and functional deficits of surviving cells.
evidence: Supported by citations throughout the manuscript and is a central premise of the study.

claim: Memory CD8 T cells provide rapid cytolysis and cytokine production following re-encounter with their cognate antigen to promote long-term immunity.
source: Memory CD8 T cells provide rapid cytolysis and cytokine production following re-encounter with their cognate antigen to promote long-term immunity, and CD8 T cell impairment due to sepsis can pre-dispose individuals to re-infection.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about memory CD8 T cell function.

claim: CD8 T cell impairment due to sepsis can pre-dispose individuals to re-infection.
source: Memory CD8 T cells provide rapid cytolysis and cytokine production following re-encounter with their cognate antigen to promote long-term immunity, and CD8 T cell impairment due to sepsis can pre-dispose individuals to re-infection.
evidence: Supported by citations in the manuscript and is a premise of the study.

claim: Central memory CD8 T cells (TCM) from septic patients proliferate more than those from healthy individuals.
source: Here, we observed that central memory CD8 T cells (TCM) from septic patients proliferate more than those from healthy individuals.
evidence: Supported by data presented in Figure 1e showing increased Ki67 expression in TCM from septic patients.

claim: TCM proliferation is associated with numerical recovery of pathogen-specific memory CD8 T cells following sepsis-induced lymphopenia.
source: Utilizing LCMV immune mice and a CLP model to induce sepsis, we demonstrated that TCM proliferation is associated with numerical recovery of pathogen-specific memory CD8 T cells following sepsis-induced lymphopenia.
evidence: Supported by data in Figures 2 and 4 showing proliferation and numeric recovery.

claim: Increased proliferation leads to changes in composition of memory CD8 T cell compartment and altered tissue localization.
source: This increased proliferation leads to changes in composition of memory CD8 T cell compartment and altered tissue localization.
evidence: Supported by data in Figures 3 and 4 showing phenotypic changes and altered tissue distribution.

claim: Memory CD8 T cells from sepsis survivors have an altered transcriptional profile and chromatin accessibility indicating long-lasting T cell intrinsic changes.
source: Further, memory CD8 T cells from sepsis survivors have an altered transcriptional profile and chromatin accessibility indicating long-lasting T cell intrinsic changes.
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq and ATAC-seq data presented in Figures 5 and 6.

claim: Sepsis-induced changes in the composition of the memory CD8 T cell pool and transcriptional landscape culminate in altered T cell function and reduced capacity to control L. monocytogenes infection.
source: The sepsis-induced changes in the composition of the memory CD8 T cell pool and transcriptional landscape culminated in altered T cell function and reduced capacity to control L. monocytogenes infection.
evidence: Supported by functional data in Figure 7 showing reduced bacterial control.

claim: Sepsis leads to long-term alterations in memory CD8 T cell phenotype, protective function and localization potentially changing host capacity to respond to re-infection.
source: Thus, sepsis leads to long-term alterations in memory CD8 T cell phenotype, protective function and localization potentially changing host capacity to respond to re-infection.
evidence: This is the main conclusion supported by all data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Nine people develop sepsis every 6 seconds and two of those individuals die.
source: Sepsis leads to a substantial global health and economic burden wherein nine people develop sepsis every 6 s and two of those individuals die (Rudd et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Rudd et al., 2020.

claim: In the United States the cost to treat sepsis is >$20 billion with a mortality rate of ~20%.
source: In the United States alone the cost to treat sepsis is >$20 billion with a mortality rate of ~20 % (CDC, 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to CDC, 2020.

claim: Sepsis mortality rate had been at ~50% over the last 30 years before recent improvements.
source: While a 20 % mortality rate is high, it is also a vast improvement over the last 30 years where mortality had been at ~50 % (Dombrovskiy et al., 2007; Gaieski et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to Dombrovskiy et al., 2007 and Gaieski et al., 2013.

claim: The reduction in mortality rate has largely been through early intervention.
source: This reduction in mortality rate has largely been through early intervention as the complexity of the cytokine storm has, dishearteningly, lead to the failure of >100 phase II and III clinical trials targeting the pro-inflammatory aspects of the cytokine storm (Marshall, 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Marshall, 2014.

claim: More than 100 phase II and III clinical trials targeting the pro-inflammatory aspects of the cytokine storm have failed.
source: This reduction in mortality rate has largely been through early intervention as the complexity of the cytokine storm has, dishearteningly, lead to the failure of >100 phase II and III clinical trials targeting the pro-inflammatory aspects of the cytokine storm (Marshall, 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Marshall, 2014.

claim: Previously septic individuals are at increased risk for mortality even after surviving the cytokine storm.
source: Yet, even as survival of the cytokine storm has increased it has also become apparent that previously septic individuals are still at increased risk for mortality, this defines the sepsis-induced immunoparalysis state (Delano and Ward, 2016a; Delano and Ward, 2016b; Dombrovskiy et al., 2007; Donnelly et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations.

claim: Sepsis-induced immunoparalysis is characterized by an increased susceptibility to both new and previously encountered unrelated infections and cancer.
source: Sepsis-induced immunoparalysis is characterized by an increased susceptibility to both new and previously encountered unrelated infections and cancer (Danahy et al., 2019; Jensen et al., 2018a; Kutza et al., 1998; Walton et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations.

claim: Sepsis-induced immunoparalysis reduces susceptibility to development of autoimmunity.
source: Alternately, sepsis-induced immunoparalysis reduces susceptibility to development of autoimmunity, cumulatively demonstrating immunologic impairment (Jensen et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Jensen et al., 2020.

claim: The majority of sepsis-associated mortality is late mortality secondary to the cytokine storm.
source: These profound impairments are sufficient to reduce the 5 year survival of septic cohorts, relative to non-septic cohorts; consequently, the majority of sepsis-associated mortality is late mortality secondary to the cytokine storm (Dombrovskiy et al., 2007; Donnelly et al., 2015; Gaieski et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations.

claim: Immunologic impairment in sepsis is typified by transient lymphopenia and reduced capacity of various surviving lymphocyte populations to perform effector function.
source: This immunologic impairment is typified by transient lymphopenia and reduced capacity of various surviving lymphocyte populations to perform effector function (Hotchkiss et al., 2016; Hotchkiss et al., 2013), including CD4 (Cabrera-Perez et al., 2014; Cabrera-Perez et al., 2015; Chen et al., 2017; Jensen et al., 2020; Martin et al., 2020; Sjaastad et al., 2020b) and CD8 T cells (Condotta et al., 2013; Danahy et al., 2017; Danahy et al., 2019; Duong et al., 2014; Serbanescu et al., 2016; Xie et al., 2019), B cells (Hotchkiss et al., 2001; Sjaastad et al., 2018; Unsinger et al., 2010), NK cells (Hou et al., 2014; Jensen et al., 2021b; Jensen et al., 2018b; Souza-Fonseca-Guimaraes et al., 2012), and dendritic cells (DCs) (Poehlmann et al., 2009; Roquilly et al., 2017; Strother et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by extensive citations for each cell type mentioned.

claim: Sepsis-induced lymphopenia impacts both memory and naïve CD8 T cells early after sepsis.
source: Specifically, sepsis-induced lymphopenia impacts both memory and naïve CD8 T cells early after sepsis (Condotta et al., 2015; Condotta et al., 2013; Duong et al., 2014; Jensen et al., 2018a; Markwart et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations.

claim: Memory CD8 T cells that survive the cytokine storm are less capable of undergoing antigen-dependent effector function and responding to inflammatory cues.
source: Additionally, those memory CD8 T cells that survive the cytokine storm are less capable of undergoing antigen-dependent effector function and responding to inflammatory cues (bystander activation).
evidence: This is stated as an established finding, likely supported by prior work cited in the manuscript.

claim: Intrinsic impairments in conjunction with numeric deficits reduce host capacity to control both infection and cancer.
source: These intrinsic impairments, in conjunction with the numeric deficits imposed by the lymphopenic environment, reduce host capacity to control both infection (i.e. viral and bacterial) and cancer (Danahy et al., 2017; Danahy et al., 2019; Duong et al., 2014; Gurung et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations.

claim: Extrinsic factors such as reduced integrin expression on endothelia or altered monocyte/macrophage activity can influence CD8 T cell capacity to migrate into sites of infection.
source: Additionally, extrinsic factors, such as reduced integrin expression on endothelia (Danahy et al., 2017) or altered monocyte/ macrophage activity (Jensen et al., 2021a; Roquilly et al., 2020), can influence CD8 T cell capacity to migrate into sites of infection.
evidence: Supported by citations to Danahy et al., 2017; Jensen et al., 2021a; Roquilly et al., 2020.

claim: CD8 T cell-mediated protection can be hampered by inability of other cells to respond to inflammatory cues provided by CD8 T cells even when T cells are spared from the cytokine storm by vascular exclusion.
source: Even when T cells are spared from the cytokine storm by vascular exclusion (i.e. tissue residence) CD8 T cell-mediated protection can be hampered by inability of other cells (e.g. endothelia) to respond to the inflammatory cues provided by CD8 T cells (Danahy et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Danahy et al., 2017.

claim: Sepsis-induced impairments are long-lasting and may not be consistent across time.
source: However, sepsis-induced impairments are long-lasting and may not be consistent across time (Jensen et al., 2018a).
evidence: Supported by citation to Jensen et al., 2018a.

claim: The lymphopenic environment is transient yet the ability to control cancer can remain reduced long after numeric recovery is complete.
source: Specifically, the lymphopenic environment is transient yet the ability to control cancer can remain reduced long after numeric recovery is complete (Danahy et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Danahy et al., 2019.

claim: There was no difference in the frequency of CD8 T cells among lymphocytes between septic patients and healthy controls.
source: While there was not a difference in the frequency of CD8 T cells among lymphocytes between septic patients and healthy controls (Figure 1a and b), there was a cohort of septic patients with a substantially reduced number of CD8 T cells per mL of blood (Figure 1c) reflecting the sepsis-induced lymphopenia.
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 1a and b.

claim: There was a cohort of septic patients with a substantially reduced number of CD8 T cells per mL of blood reflecting sepsis-induced lymphopenia.
source: While there was not a difference in the frequency of CD8 T cells among lymphocytes between septic patients and healthy controls (Figure 1a and b), there was a cohort of septic patients with a substantially reduced number of CD8 T cells per mL of blood (Figure 1c) reflecting the sepsis-induced lymphopenia.
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 1c.

claim: Robust induction of Ki67 expression was observed in CD8 T cells from septic patients regardless of degree of lymphopenia.
source: Notably, robust induction of Ki67 expression, a marker of recent proliferation, by CD8 T cells (Figure 1a and d) was observed, regardless of degree of lymphopenia.
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 1a and d.

claim: There was robust proliferation among naïve, TCM, and TSCM CD8 T cells in septic patients.
source: Intriguingly, robust proliferation among naïve, TCM, and TSCM CD8 T cells was observed, suggesting proliferation may reflect numerical recovery after sepsis-induced lymphopenia (Figure 1e).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 1e.

claim: There was not a significant increase in Ki67+ TEM CD8 T cells from septic patients.
source: Notably, there was not a significant increase in Ki67+ TEM CD8 T cells from septic patients (Figure 1e).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 1e.

claim: There was a modest, although not statistically different, increase in the frequency of both TCM and TSCM CD8 T cells in septic patients relative to healthy controls.
source: Indeed, there was a modest, although not statistically different, increase in the frequency of both TCM and TSCM CD8 T cells in septic patients, relative to healthy controls, even at this early time point (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1a.

claim: TCM was the most prominent among cells that recently proliferated in septic patients.
source: Importantly, when evaluating the representation of CD8 T cell subsets among Ki67-expressing CD8 T cells, TCM and TSCM CD8 T cells were not proportionally increased (Figure 1—figure supplement 1b), with TCM being the most prominent among cells that recently proliferated.
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1b.

claim: Naïve and Ag-exp cells were impacted to the same degree by sepsis-induced lymphopenia.
source: Following septic insult, the lymphopenic state impacted naïve and Ag-exp cells to the same degree (Figure 2c), as has been previously reported (Condotta et al., 2013; Duong et al., 2014; Jensen et al., 2018a).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 2c and citations to prior work.

claim: Memory P14 CD8 T cells were similarly susceptible to sepsis-induced lymphopenia as endogenous Ag-exp cells.
source: Importantly, the memory P14 CD8 T cells were similarly susceptible to sepsis-induced lymphopenia as the endogenous Ag-exp cells (Figure 2c).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 2c.

claim: There was induction of Ki67 expression by memory P14 CD8 T cells after sepsis.
source: Additionally, there was induction of Ki67 expression by memory P14 CD8 T cells after sepsis (Figure 2d and e), demonstrating that the P14 CD8 T cells can be used to model the influence of sepsis on pre-existing memory CD8 T cells.
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 2d and e.

claim: Numeric loss and recovery of P14 CD8 T cells was observed in CLP hosts.
source: When the number of memory P14 CD8 T cells per mL of blood was quantified, we observed numeric loss and recovery of P14 CD8 T cells in CLP hosts (Figure 2f), similar to prior reports of homeostatic proliferation following sepsis-induced lymphopenia (Unsinger et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 2f and citation to Unsinger et al., 2009.

claim: Sham and CLP hosts had differential representation of FlowSOM-defined clusters 6 and 8.
source: Notably, Sham and CLP hosts had differential representation of two of the most prominent clusters (6 and 8) with cluster six being enriched in Sham P14 CD8 T cells and cluster eight in CLP P14 CD8 T cells (Figure 3d and e).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 3d and e.

claim: Memory P14 CD8 T cells enriched in Sham mice (cluster 6) were CD62L-KLRG1+CD127-CX3CR1+CXCR3lo.
source: Memory P14 CD8 T cells enriched in Sham mice (cluster 6) were CD62L-KLRG1+CD127-CX3CR1+CXCR3lo, while memory P14 CD8 T cells enriched in CLP mice (cluster 8) were CD62L+KLRG1-CD127+CX3CR1-CXCR3lo/med (Figure 3h).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 3h.

claim: Memory P14 CD8 T cells enriched in CLP mice (cluster 8) were CD62L+KLRG1-CD127+CX3CR1-CXCR3lo/med.
source: Memory P14 CD8 T cells enriched in Sham mice (cluster 6) were CD62L-KLRG1+CD127-CX3CR1+CXCR3lo, while memory P14 CD8 T cells enriched in CLP mice (cluster 8) were CD62L+KLRG1-CD127+CX3CR1-CXCR3lo/med (Figure 3h).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 3h.

claim: Clusters 6 and 8 define TEM and TCM CD8 T cells, respectively.
source: Clusters 6 and 8 therefore appear to define TEM and TCM CD8 T cells, respectively.
evidence: This is an inference based on the phenotypic markers shown in Figure 3h and established knowledge of TEM and TCM phenotypes.

claim: CLP P14 CD8 T cells are enriched for TCM with a reduced representation of TEM.
source: Thus, CLP P14 CD8 T cells are enriched for TCM with a reduced representation of TEM, corresponding to the increased proliferation of CD8 TCM observed in septic patients (Figure 1e; Figure 1—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 3 and referenced back to Figure 1.

claim: Both TCM and TEM proliferated in CLP hosts greater than their Sham counterparts following lymphopenia.
source: Indeed, both TCM and TEM proliferated in CLP hosts greater than their Sham counterparts, following lymphopenia (Figure 4b).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 4b.

claim: P14 CD8 TCM cells proliferated more robustly than their TEM counterparts in CLP hosts.
source: However, P14 CD8 TCM cells proliferated more robustly than their TEM counterparts in CLP hosts.
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 4b.

claim: P14 CD8 TCM cells proliferated more than their TEM counterparts in Sham hosts across all timepoints.
source: Importantly, P14 CD8 TCM cells proliferated more than their TEM counterparts in Sham hosts across all timepoints, consistent with prior reports of higher homeostatic proliferation among TCM cells (Wherry et al., 2003).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 4b and citation to Wherry et al., 2003.

claim: Elevated proliferation was observed in both TCM and TEM P14 CD8 T cells from CLP hosts relative to Sham hosts as measured by BrdU incorporation.
source: Similar to the results with Ki67, elevated proliferation was observed in both TCM and TEM P14 CD8 T cells from CLP hosts, relative to Sham hosts (Figure 4d).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 4d.

claim: P14 CD8 TCM cells had higher incorporation of BrdU relative to TEM counterparts in both Sham and CLP hosts.
source: Additionally, P14 CD8 TCM cells had higher incorporation of BrdU (relative to TEM counterparts) in both Sham and CLP hosts with P14 CD8 TCM cells from CLP hosts having the highest degree of BrdU incorporation.
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 4d.

claim: There was an increase in the frequency of TCM among P14 CD8 T cells at D16 post-surgery.
source: This proliferative difference was further associated with an increase in the frequency of TCM among P14 CD8 T cells at D16 post-surgery, the time at which BrdU assessment was performed (Figure 4e).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 4e.

claim: The ratio of P14 CD8 T cells among lymphocytes in the liver and PBL relative to the spleen had a trending reduction in CLP hosts compared to Sham hosts.
source: Indeed, the ratio of P14 CD8 T cells among lymphocytes in the liver and PBL, relative to the spleen, had a trending reduction in CLP hosts, compared to Sham hosts (Figure 4g).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 4g.

claim: The ratio of P14 CD8 T cells among lymphocytes in the medLN and mesLN relative to the spleen were significantly increased in CLP hosts compared to Sham hosts.
source: Conversely, the ratio of P14 CD8 T cells among lymphocytes in the medLN and mesLN relative to the spleen, were significantly increased in CLP hosts, compared to Sham hosts.
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 4g.

claim: Numerous transcriptional differences between Sham and CLP groups at D1 and D31 were identified.
source: Numerous transcriptional differences between the four groups were identified (Figure 5b–d).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5b-d.

claim: There was clear distinction between the Sham and CLP groups at each timepoint by principal component analysis.
source: Notably, when evaluated by principal component analysis (PCA) there was clear distinction between the Sham and CLP groups at each timepoint (Figure 5b); however, this distinction narrowed at D31 relative to D1 potentially reflecting some degree of recovery from the initial the cytokine storm.
evidence: Supported by PCA data shown in Figure 5b.

claim: 269 gene changes (174 down, 95 up) were present at D31 post-surgery in CLP hosts relative to Sham controls.
source: Importantly, numerous gene changes (269 total; 174 down, 95up) were present at D31 post-surgery in CLP hosts, relative to Sham controls (Figure 5c and d).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5c and d.

claim: 99 of the 269 transcriptional differences between Sham and CLP memory P14 CD8 T cells at D31 were associated with time-dependent changes in memory.
source: These changes constituted 99 of the 269 transcriptional (Table 2) differences between Sham and CLP memory P14 CD8 T cells at D31 and validate the observations in the prior figures of more rapid adoption of time-dependent changes in memory (i.e. conversion to central memory) (e.g. changes in clusters 6 and 8 of Figure 3).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5e and Table 2.

claim: 113 of the 269 gene changes observed at D31 constituted a sepsis-induced transcriptional 'scar'.
source: This sepsis-induced 'scar' constituted 113 of the 269 gene changes observed (Table 2) and demonstrates that some of the transcriptional changes evoked early after sepsis persist.
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5e and Table 2.

claim: 57 gene changes were neither associated with time-dependent changes in CD8 T cell memory nor with early sepsis induced changes.
source: Finally, there remained a third cluster of 57 gene changes (Table 2) that were neither associated with time-dependent changes in CD8 T cell memory nor were they associated with the early sepsis induced changes to memory CD8 T cells.
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5e and Table 2.

claim: 1646 chromatin accessibility peaks were differentially expressed between Sham and CLP P14 CD8 T cells at D31.
source: While 1646 peaks were differentially expressed, the changes observed were predominantly more peaks (more accessibility) in CLP hosts (Figure 5g).
evidence: Supported by ATAC-seq data shown in Figure 5g.

claim: Changes in chromatin accessibility were predominantly more peaks (more accessibility) in CLP hosts.
source: While 1646 peaks were differentially expressed, the changes observed were predominantly more peaks (more accessibility) in CLP hosts (Figure 5g).
evidence: Supported by ATAC-seq data shown in Figure 5g.

claim: There were genes whose chromatin accessibility and transcription is concordant between Sham and CLP P14 CD8 T cells.
source: Indeed, there were genes whose chromatin accessibility and transcription is concordant.
evidence: Supported by comparison of RNA-seq and ATAC-seq data shown in Figure 5h and i.

claim: P2r×7, Rad51, and Bub1b have prior association with CD8 T cell survival, DNA damage repair, and cell cycling.
source: Among these P2r×7, Rad51, and Bub1b all have prior association with CD8 T cell survival, DNA damage repair, and cell cycling (Baek et al., 2003; Borges da Silva et al., 2018; Yamamoto et al., 1996).
evidence: Supported by citations to Baek et al., 2003; Borges da Silva et al., 2018; Yamamoto et al., 1996.

claim: The increased accessibility at the Sell locus corresponds to increased transcription at that locus.
source: Thus, the increased accessibility at the Sell locus corresponds to increased transcription at that locus (Figure 5j) and a subsequent increase in the expression of CD62L (Figure 4).
evidence: Supported by comparison of ATAC-seq and RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5i, j and phenotypic data in Figure 4.

claim: There was decreased expression of Cx3cr1 and Klrg1 in CLP P14 CD8 T cells relative to Sham.
source: Importantly, the transcription of the additional phenotypic distinctions observed in Figure 3 largely conformed wherein there was decreased expression of Cx3cr1 and Klrg1 (Figure 5j), though no change in expression was observed for other markers such Cxcr3 and Il7r.
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5j.

claim: The top five positively enriched KEGG pathways in CLP P14 CD8 T cells showed an obvious trend toward cell cycling.
source: When evaluating the top five positively enriched KEGG pathways in CLP P14 CD8 T cells, there was an obvious trend toward cell cycling (Figure 6a).
evidence: Supported by GSEA data shown in Figure 6a.

claim: The top five positively enriched KEGG pathways in CLP P14 CD8 T cells included: KEGG_Ribosome, _DNA_Replication, _Nucleotide_Excision_Repair, _Proteasome, and _Cell_Cycle.
source: Specifically, the pathways included: KEGG_Ribosome, _DNA_Replication, _Nucleotide_Excision_Repair, _Proteasome, and _Cell_Cycle.
evidence: Supported by GSEA data shown in Figure 6a.

claim: There was substantial enrichment of ribosomal proteins in CLP P14 CD8 T cells.
source: A critical example of this is the substantial enrichment of ribosomal proteins (Figure 6b and c), putatively necessary for increased translational output during proliferation.
evidence: Supported by GSEA data shown in Figure 6b and c.

claim: Several pathways were negatively enriched in CLP P14 CD8 T cells including: KEGG_Complement_And_Coagulation_Cascades, _Glycerophopholipid_Metabolism, _FC_Gamma_R_Mediated_Phagocytosis, _Cell_Adhesion_Molecules_CAMS, and _FC_Epsilon_RI_Signaling_Pathway.
source: Conversely, several pathways were also negatively enriched in CLP P14 CD8 T cells (positively enriched in Sham), including: KEGG_Complement_And_Coagulation_Cascades, _Glycerophopholipid_Metabolism, _FC_Gamma_R_Mediated_Phagocytosis, _Cell_Adhesion_Molecules_CAMS, and _FC_Epsilon_RI_Signaling_Pathway (Figure 6d).
evidence: Supported by GSEA data shown in Figure 6d.

claim: Reduced expression of additional integrins was observed in CLP P14 CD8 T cells.
source: Given that integrin expression was also identified among the concordant genes in Figure 5g, gene enrichment in KEGG_Cell_Adhesion_Molecules_CAMS was evaluated and reduced expression of additional integrins was observed (Figure 6e and f).
evidence: Supported by GSEA data shown in Figure 6e and f.

claim: P14s from Sham hosts were biased toward effector CD8 T cells while P14s from CLP hosts were biased toward memory CD8 T cells when compared to the KAECH_DAY15_EFF_VS_MEMORY_CD8_TCELL dataset.
source: Further, when we compared the transcriptional changes between Sham D31 and CLP D31 with the published data set KAECH_DAY15_EFF_VS_MEMORY_CD8_TCELL we observed that P14s from Sham hosts were biased toward effector CD8 T cells while the P14s from CLP hosts were biased toward memory CD8 T cells, mirroring the shift from effector to central CD8 T cell memory (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by GSEA data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Impairment in adherence capacity was observed in P14 CD8 T cells from CLP hosts under limiting stimulation conditions.
source: Notably, impairment in adherence capacity was observed in P14 CD8 T cells from CLP hosts under limiting stimulation conditions (low αCD3 concentration; Figure 7—figure supplement 1b, c); however, when stimulation was not limiting (high αCD3 concentration) Sham and CLP P14 CD8 T cells were equally capable of undergoing TCR-dependent adhesion.
evidence: Supported by adhesion assay data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1b, c.

claim: Despite equal capability to adhere there remained a deficit in the ability to cluster AKT at the cell membrane following TCR stimulation in CLP P14 CD8 T cells.
source: Importantly, despite equal capability to adhere there remained a deficit in the ability to cluster AKT at the cell membrane following TCR stimulation (Figure 7—figure supplement 1d, e).
evidence: Supported by TIRF microscopy data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1d, e.

claim: There was no deficiency in capacity to produce IFNγ by P14 CD8 T cells from CLP hosts.
source: Intriguingly, there was no deficiency in capacity to produce IFNγ, yet P14 CD8 T cells from CLP hosts actually had a higher capacity to produce IL-2 (Figure 7b–d).
evidence: Supported by cytokine production data shown in Figure 7b-d.

claim: P14 CD8 T cells from CLP hosts had a higher capacity to produce IL-2.
source: Intriguingly, there was no deficiency in capacity to produce IFNγ, yet P14 CD8 T cells from CLP hosts actually had a higher capacity to produce IL-2 (Figure 7b–d).
evidence: Supported by cytokine production data shown in Figure 7b-d.

claim: Recipients that received memory P14 CD8 T cells from either Sham or CLP hosts more robustly controlled L.m. infection than naive hosts that did not receive any memory CD8 T cells.
source: Recipients that received memory P14 CD8 T cells from either Sham or CLP hosts more robustly controlled L.m. infection than the naive hosts that did not receive any memory CD8 T cells (Figure 7f and g).
evidence: Supported by bacterial burden data shown in Figure 7f and g.

claim: Memory P14 CD8 T cells from Sham recipients were significantly better at controlling L.m. than those from CLP recipients with 77- and 20-fold differences in control in the liver and spleen, respectively.
source: However, memory P14 CD8 T cells from Sham recipients were significantly better at controlling L.m. than those from CLP recipients; 77- and 20-fold differences control in the liver and spleen, respectively (Figure 7f and g).
evidence: Supported by bacterial burden data shown in Figure 7f and g.

claim: TCM have a higher capacity to undergo homeostatic proliferation relative to TEM.
source: TCM have a higher capacity to undergo homeostatic proliferation, relative to TEM, which accounts for the gradual shift toward TCM with time after antigen encounter (Martin and Badovinac, 2018; Martin et al., 2015; Wherry et al., 2003).
evidence: Supported by citations to Martin and Badovinac, 2018; Martin et al., 2015; Wherry et al., 2003.

claim: TCM preferentially localizes to lymphatic tissue while TEM preferentially circulates and traverse non-lymphatic tissue.
source: In addition to differential capacity to undergo homeostatic proliferation TCM and TEM have different localization throughout the body. TCM preferentially localizes to lymphatic tissue while TEM preferentially circulates and traverse non-lymphatic tissue (Gerlach et al., 2016; Masopust et al., 2001; Mueller et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to Gerlach et al., 2016; Masopust et al., 2001; Mueller et al., 2013.

claim: TRM were not susceptible to sepsis-induced lymphopenia due to their exclusion from the vasculature.
source: Danahy et al. previously demonstrated that TRM were not susceptible to sepsis-induced lymphopenia, due to their exclusion from the vasculature (Danahy et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Danahy et al., 2017.

claim: Lung TRM are seeded from circulating TEM.
source: Specifically, Slütter et al. demonstrated that lung TRM are seeded from circulating TEM (Slütter et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Slütter et al., 2017.

claim: TEM more effectively control virulent Listeria monocytogenes infection compared to TCM.
source: Nolz et al. previously demonstrated that TEM more effectively control virulent Listeria monocytogenes (L.m.) infection compared to TCM (Nolz and Harty, 2011), likely due to localization of cells in either non-lymphoid tissues (critically the liver) or lymphoid tissues, respectively.
evidence: Supported by citation to Nolz and Harty, 2011.

claim: Naïve cells undergo antigen-independent proliferation in lymphopenic environments such as Rag-/- or irradiated hosts.
source: Indeed, naive cells undergo antigen-independent proliferation in other lymphopenic environments, such as Rag-/- or irradiated hosts, wherein they adopt conventional markers of antigen experience along with some effector functionality (Cheung et al., 2009; Pribikova et al., 2018; Unsinger et al., 2009; White et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to Cheung et al., 2009; Pribikova et al., 2018; Unsinger et al., 2009; White et al., 2017.

claim: Patient cohorts did not exhibit substantial demographic differences though septic patients were severely ill as defined by APACHE II and SOFA scores.
source: Patient cohorts did not exhibit substantial demographic differences though septic patients were severely ill, as defined by APACHE II and SOFA scores (Table 1).
evidence: Supported by demographic data shown in Table 1.

claim: Admission time may not correspond to the onset of sepsis such that admitted patients may have not yet experienced or already recovered from sepsis-associated lymphopenia.
source: It is relevant to consider that admission time may not correspond to the onset of sepsis such that admitted patients may have not yet experienced or already recovered from sepsis-associated lymphopenia.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the timing of patient sampling.

claim: Numeric variability in samples may reflect a broad range of insult and recovery within the 24 hr of admission.
source: Thus, numeric variability in samples may reflect a broad range of insult and recovery within the 24 hr of admission.
evidence: This is an inference based on the variability observed in patient data.

claim: The biasing toward TCM may pose a particular problem for TRM due to reduced seeding of cells during the lymphopenic state and reduced TEM pool from which to seed the TRM.
source: Specifically, Slütter et al. demonstrated that lung TRM are seeded from circulating TEM (Slütter et al., 2017). Thus, the challenge to the TRM may be twofold: (1) the reduced seeding of cells during the lymphopenic state and (2) reduced TEM pool from which to seed the TRM.
evidence: This is an inference based on the shift toward TCM and the known biology of TRM seeding.

claim: The reduction in TEM may culminate in a more rapid waning of lung TRM and reinforce susceptibility to previously encountered infections.
source: This reduction may culminate in a more rapid waning of lung TRM and reinforce susceptibility to previously encountered infections.
evidence: This is a speculative inference about the consequences of reduced TEM.

claim: The detrimental effects of sepsis on memory CD8 T cells may also be relevant to other major inflammatory events and poorly controlled infections.
source: Moreover, the detrimental effects of sepsis on memory CD8 T cells may also be relevant to other major inflammatory events and poorly controlled infections (e.g. SARS-CoV-2) and should be considerations in the long-term consequences for similarly impacted individuals (Li et al., 2020; Sariol and Perlman, 2020).
evidence: This is a speculative statement supported by citations to Li et al., 2020 and Sariol and Perlman, 2020.

claim: Infections for which TCM can provide critical control may be unimpaired or even enhanced in the post-septic environment.
source: Thus, infections for which TCM can provide critical control may be unimpaired or even enhanced in the post-septic environment.
evidence: This is a speculative inference about potential benefits of the shift toward TCM.

claim: It remains possible that other T cell populations may bias toward effector memory depending on their antigen specificity.
source: Additionally, while our interrogation focused on a shift of pre-existing memory CD8 T cells toward a central memory phenotype, it remains possible that other T cell populations (e.g. different antigen specificities) may bias toward effector memory.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential variability in responses.

claim: Memory T cell populations whose TCR has some low degree of cross reactivity with antigens present on microbes released during the septic event may bias toward effector memory.
source: This may be particularly relevant to memory T cell populations whose TCR has some low degree of cross reactivity with antigens present on microbes released during the septic event.
evidence: This is a speculative inference about potential mechanisms for differential responses.

claim: Future studies should consider additional interrogation of mechanisms by which the immune system is altered beyond detrimental aspects.
source: Therefore, future studies should consider additional interrogation of mechanisms by which the immune system is altered beyond detrimental aspects.
evidence: This is a recommendation for future research.

claim: Proliferation by naïve CD8 T cells in septic hosts suggests that CD8 T cells are proliferating in response to the lymphopenic environment.
source: The proliferation by naïve CD8 T cells in septic hosts suggests that CD8 T cells are proliferating in response to the lymphopenic environment.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed proliferation of naïve cells.

claim: The proliferation of naïve cells may alter the composition of the memory CD8 T cell compartment and shape host response to subsequent infection.
source: Thus, it may be relevant to consider how the proliferation of these cells also alter the composition of the memory CD8 T cell compartment and shapes host response to subsequent infection for which they may be specific.
evidence: This is a speculative inference about the consequences of naïve cell proliferation.

claim: Future interrogation of lasting effects will likely be required to best address the deficits that arise in the immunoparalysis state.
source: Future interrogation of these lasting effects will likely be required to best address the deficits that arise in the immunoparalysis state.
evidence: This is a recommendation for future research.

claim: One potential application may be in the promotion of TCM over TEM, or vice versa, for specific vaccination strategies.
source: One such example may be in the promotion of TCM over TEM, or vice versa, for specific vaccination strategies.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential applications.
